alex: bringing up a new compact embedding 'wavelet-emb' on staging (int6 per-channel). ran an initial recall/cluster smoke against the wiki holdout and numbers look off vs our 768 baseline :thinking_face:
priya: can you paste the quick numbers and the exact eval command? :eyes:
alex: sure, quick paste below:
```
Model: wavelet-emb (dim=512, quant=int6_pc)
Holdout: wiki-10k
Baseline (bert-embed-768): recall@1=0.71 recall@10=0.95 silhouette=0.27
Wavelet (staging): recall@1=0.58 recall@10=0.89 silhouette=0.12
```
Command: `python eval/recall.py --model wavelet-emb --quant int6_pc --holdout wiki-10k --batch 256 --seed 42`
dan: whoa recall@1 drop is notable. is the preprocessing identical? tokenization/truncation?
azlex: preprocessing is the same pipeline, config link: https://s3.redwood-internal/wavelet/configs/wavelet-staging.json
zoe: dim mismatch might bite — 512 vs 768 could affect nearest neighbor geometry. did you try L2-normalize embeddings?
alex: yes L2 applied. I also tried cosine and dot; same relative drop. embedding norms roughly stable.
priya: any loss in micro-batch KVCACHE ordering or batching differences that could change RNG?
dan: also ask whether quantized op ordering differs — rounding bias can break small nearest-neighbor margins. what's the average pairwise distance distribution?
alex: ran a quick dist histogram, attaching toplines:
```
Baseline avg intra-cluster dist=0.42 inter=1.13
Wavelet avg intra=0.63 inter=1.05
```
So intra-cluster got much worse.
zoe: hmm that suggests representation collapsed toward higher dispersion inside clusters. could be embedding head normalization or a bug in the projector layer after quantization.
priya: try two quick checks: 1) run the model unquantized (fp16) on same checkpoint to see if architecture change vs quantization is culprit, 2) run baseline model down-projected to 512 (PCA) to estimate dim effect.
alex: starting fp16 run now (ETA ~12m), and will run baseline->PCA next. posting logs to s3 when done.
ci-bot: bench-run uploaded - s3://rwd-internal/evals/wavelet/4299998888/ (files: recall.json, dists.csv, pca-probe.json) :thumbsup:
priya: thanks. if fp16 matches baseline-ish, it's quant. if fp16 still low, it's model itself.
dan: also try per-channel vs symmetric int6 variants (we've seen symmetric sometimes degrade for projected heads).

alex: will queue int6_sym and int8_pc runs. updating thread with numbers as they come.
(12m later)
alex: fp16 run results:
```
Wavelet fp16: recall@1=0.69 recall@10=0.94 silhouette=0.25
```
So fp16 is close to baseline. quant seems to be the main culprit.
zoe: ok that narrows it. try int6 symmetric and int8 per-channel as sanity checks. also run a tiny calibration pass (recalib with 10k samples) — sometimes our defaults mis-center biases.
alex: int6_sym queued, int8_pc queued, and ran a quick calib with 10k samples.
(another 8m)
alex: short results:
```
int6_pc (orig): recall@1=0.58 recall@10=0.89
int6_sym: recall@1=0.65 recall@10=0.92
int8_pc: recall@1=0.68 recall@10=0.94
calibrated int6_pc: recall@1=0.62 recall@10=0.91
```
So int6_sym and int8_pc both improve; calibration helps a bit.
priya: great. that suggests quantization error & dynamic range choice. int6_pc still borderline. tradeoff: int6 better cost but riskier; int8_pc seems safe. we should add automatic calibration step to int6 pipeline and compare cost delta.
dan: we should also run a micro-A/B test on a downstream reranker pipeline to measure real product impact for the int6 vs int8 choices. recall numbers are a proxy.
alex: agree. for short-term I propose: default to int8_pc for staging, keep int6_pc behind a rollout with calibration and extra evals (silhouette + recall@1 on 5 holdouts).
zoe: +1. Also let's add a diagnostic that logs avg per-dimension quant error and top-100 neighbor shifts for sample queries (to detect catastrophic rank flips).
priya: I'll open a small PR with the calibration hook and a rollout checklist. alex can you attach the eval artifacts and the small script to compute neighbor-shift?
alex: done — s3 link in thread, and I pushed the neighbor-shift script to the wavelet repo under evals/neighbor_shift.py.
ci-bot: PR 8142 opened by priya: "wavelet: add int6 calibration + rollout checklist" (link)
priya: ok I'll coordinate canary rollout after we get ops thumbs. tagging @dan for canary approval.
dan: will review canary checklist. seems reasonable to keep int8 default until we vet int6 with more holdouts.
alex: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short doc summarizing cost vs quality tradeoffs and the planned rollout phases. :rocket:
